title: The Impact of Education on Chronic Disease Risk

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Causal method: Two-Stage Least Squares (IV).  
Rationale: Years of education (x) may be correlated with unobserved health endowments or family background that also affect the probability of a chronic disease (y), creating endogeneity. Quarter-of-birth (z) is plausibly exogenous, affects schooling through compulsory-schooling laws, and therefore serves as an instrument.  

Key assumptions  
• Relevance: Quarter-of-birth must shift years of education (first-stage F-stat ≳ 10).  
• Exclusion restriction: Quarter-of-birth affects chronic-disease risk only through its impact on education, conditional on controls.  
• Monotonicity/No defiers: Being born in an “early” quarter does not reduce education for anyone who would otherwise stay in school longer.  

## 2. R Code
```r
############################################################
#  Impact of Education on Chronic Disease Risk – IV analysis
#  File: experiments/exp_b/data/s72_data.csv
############################################################

# Packages -------------------------------------------------
required <- c("readr", "AER", "sandwich", "lmtest")
for(p in required){
  if(!requireNamespace(p, quietly = TRUE)) install.packages(p)
  library(p, character.only = TRUE)
}

# 1. Read data --------------------------------------------
dat <- read_csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s72_data.csv",
                col_types = cols(
                  y = col_double(),
                  x = col_double(),
                  z = col_integer(),
                  controls = col_double()
                ))

# 2. OLS benchmark ----------------------------------------
ols <- lm(y ~ x + controls, data = dat)
cat("\n=== OLS (naïve) ===\n")
coeftest(ols, vcov = vcovHC(ols, type = "HC1")) |> print()

# 3. 2SLS / IV --------------------------------------------
iv  <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | z + controls, data = dat)

# Robust (HC1) s.e.
iv_robust <- coeftest(iv, vcov = vcovHC(iv, type = "HC1"))

cat("\n=== IV results (robust s.e.) ===\n")
print(iv_robust)

# 4. First-stage diagnostics ------------------------------
# Extracting first-stage F statistic
iv_diag <- summary(iv, diagnostics = TRUE)
cat("\n--- First-stage F-statistic on instrument (relevance) ---\n")
print(iv_diag$diagnostics["Weak instruments",])

# 5. Anderson–Rubin test (weak-instrument robust) ---------
ar <- linearHypothesis(iv, "x = 0", test = "AndersonRubin")
cat("\n--- Anderson-Rubin test for significance of education ---\n")
print(ar)

# 6. Sensitivity: include quadratic control ---------------
dat$controls2 <- dat$controls^2
iv_sens <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls + controls2 | z + controls + controls2, data = dat)
cat("\n=== IV with quadratic control (robust) ===\n")
coeftest(iv_sens, vcov = vcovHC(iv_sens, type = "HC1")) |> print()

# 7. Key numerical output ---------------------------------
edu_coef <- iv_robust["x",1]        # point estimate
edu_se   <- iv_robust["x",2]        # robust s.e.
cat("\n========================================================\n")
cat("IV point estimate of effect of 1 additional year of education on chronic-disease index:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Coefficient = %.4f  (robust s.e. = %.4f)\n", edu_coef, edu_se))
cat("========================================================\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings  
Sign: Negative. More schooling is generally associated with improved health behaviours, higher earnings, and better access to information, all of which lower chronic-disease risk.  

Magnitude: For a standardised chronic-disease index, prior literature suggests roughly −0.05 to −0.10 standard-deviation change per additional year of education. With this synthetic sample I expect an IV coefficient near −0.06, with a robust standard error of about 0.02–0.03 (implying statistical significance if the instrument is strong).

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Quarter-of-birth serves as an instrument for education.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Higher educational attainment significantly reduces the risk of chronic diseases.
